summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with a history of ESRD on hemodialysis, diabetes, peripheral vascular disease with bilateral below-knee amputations, atrial fibrillation, and hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy was admitted for acute shortness of breath and fluid overload. She had been underdialyzed and reported dietary indiscretion with salty foods. She was hypertensive on arrival and treated with IV nitroglycerin and Lasix. Hemodialysis was performed, leading to symptom resolution and euvolemia. Her INR was supratherapeutic at 4.4, so warfarin was held and later resumed at discharge. Leukocytosis resolved without evidence of infection. Metoprolol was uptitrated to 100 mg twice daily for rate control. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to resume dialysis, follow a low-salt diet, and monitor INR.
